small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_P configs (64, 128) with num_warps=8 — current best caps at 32, but with POOL=4 each pool is 16 elements so TILE=BLOCK_P*16 grows fast; try BLOCK_P=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=2 and BLOCK_P=32 num_stages=3/4 to better hide the IC*KH*KW load latency.
- Split BLOCK_OC into a tunable tile (e.g. 32/64) instead of padding to next-pow2=64; with OC=64 a 32-tile with two pid_oc programs may give more parallelism (currently only N*ceil(PH*PW/BLOCK_P) = 128*128 ≈ 16k programs at BLOCK_P=16 — fine, but tiling OC enables better register pressure trade-offs).
- Hoist weight loads out of the spatial loop: load the full [BLOCK_OC, IC*KH*KW] weight tile once per program (only 64*72=4608 floats) into registers/SRAM and iterate only over input gathers — removes redundant w_ptr loads across the 9 kh/kw iterations.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an explicit im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC_tile, output-spatial tile of size BLOCK_M covering whole pool windows), with K = IC*KH*KW as the contracted dim. Use tl.dot on [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K] x [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_M] tiles — current kernel does an outer-product accumulation (w[:,None]*x[None,:]) which doesn't use tensor cores; switching to tl.dot on fp32 (or fp16 cast) should give a large speedup since conv dominates runtime.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the GEMM-K dimension (IC) is contiguous; pre-permute x once in forward. This makes the inner-K loads coalesce and enables vectorized tl.load over IC.
- Make pool fusion the epilogue of the GEMM: pick BLOCK_M = POOL*POOL*pools_per_tile so each program produces whole pool windows, applies tanh/scale/bias on the accumulator, and reduces over the POOL*POOL group before storing — same fusion boundary as now but on top of a tl.dot-based core.
